task3_min_edges_removal.description: Given the visual representation of a graph, find the minimum number of edges to remove to completely disconnect the two highlighted nodes.

no_cot.system_message: You are a third-year Computer Science student, capable of working with visual representations of graphs. In the next messages, you will be given a visual representation of a graph. In the visual representation, all nodes are yellow circles with a black border and a black letter label. Be careful: nodes are ONLY connected if there is a visible CONTINUOUS black straight line between them, even if it has bends. The absence of a line between two nodes indicates NO connection between them, and a line passing near a node WITHOUT touching its border does NOT count. Be careful of crossings between lines. - An EDGE is a black straight line that directly connects two nodes. - A PATH is a sequence of nodes where each consecutive pair is directly linked by an edge. - The LENGTH of a path is the number of edges (lines) traversed. Your task is to determine the minimum number of edges that must be removed in order to completely disconnect the two highlighted nodes (i.e., to ensure that NO path exists between them anymore). To ensure accuracy: 1. Explicitly verify that removing the selected edges breaks ALL existing paths between the two target nodes. 2. Explore the graph systematically, considering ALL possible paths between the two nodes. 3. Do not assume disconnection: rely only on the visible structure of the graph. 4. The goal is to find the minimum number of edges whose removal achieves disconnection. Only the final answer should be provided, in this format: Edges to remove: N, Cut Set: [(X, Y), (A, B), (C, D)]. If no disconnection is possible without removing one of the two highlighted nodes, which is not allowed, then return: Edges to remove: 0, Cut Set: [], Note: No disconnection is possible without removing a target node.
no_cot.user_message: Please determine the MINIMUM number of edges that must be removed in order to completely DISCONNECT the two nodes with a THICK RED border in the graph. The two target nodes cannot be removed, and your goal is to ensure that NO path exists between them after removing a set of edges. Use only the visual representation of the graph to determine your answer. Each node is labeled with a black letter, and nodes are only connected if there is a visible black line between them. Before answering, verify that: 1. Each edge in the cut set is necessary to break all paths between the two highlighted nodes. 2. There exists NO smaller set of edges that would also disconnect them. 3. The two target nodes must remain intact. Provide only the final answer in this format: Edges to remove: N, Cut Set: [(X, Y), (A, B), (C, D)].
